item.title: AIs as Modern Genies
item.description: This essay was written with Barath Raghavan, and originally appeared in Lawfare. In April, an artificial intelligence (AI) agent conducting a routine task at a company hit a snag, tried to solve it, and soon ended up deleting the company’s database along with all of its backups. In July, OpenAI asked an unreleased AI model to attempt a hacking test. Instead of staying in the isolated box the developers had put it in, the model hacked onto the open internet and into another company to steal the answers. And as reported in August, an AI agent booked someone into a full gym class by ......

item.description: A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software. This vulnerability is due to the availability of memory write commands in the UEFI Shell while UEFI Secure Boot is enabled on a device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by selecting the UE...

item.title: Cisco Secure Email Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions Ciphertext Decryption Vulnerabilities
item.description: Multiple vulnerabilities in the Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) decryption functionality of Cisco Secure Email could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to recover plain text from encrypted email messages. These vulnerabilities are due to insufficient validation of message integrity. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by using a machine-in-the-middle technique to intercept and modify traffic between email gateways. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to obtain plaintext content from the encrypted communication. There are no workarounds that ad...

item.title: Stealing AI Reasoning Traces
item.description: Interesting research: “Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs“: Abstract: Leading large language model providers now conceal their models’ step-by-step reasoning, or chain-of-thought, to protect intellectual property and limit information leakage. Rather than storing these traces server-side, providers return them to the client as blocks of encrypted text, which the client passes back with each subsequent request. Building on prior research, we identify an architectural vulnerability: these encrypted blocks are fully compatible and interchangeable across different sessions, users,...

item.title: Testing race conditions with memory access tracing and stack-based delay injection
item.description: Many security bugs are race conditions, where multi-threaded execution has to occur with the right interleaving for a negative effect to appear. This creates challenges for several use cases: Confirming bug candidates that have been discovered manually or through static analysis. Regression tests: After fixing a race condition bug, there is often no good way to write a regression test that reliably triggers the bug as part of a test suite. Automatic bug discovery, such as fuzzing: It is hard for a fuzzer to exercise all interesting interleavings of concurrent operations, or reach code paths th...

item.title: AIs Compress Exploit Timeline
item.description: Give an AI agent a mere rumor of an exploit, and it’s enough for them to find it. What’s worse, I found I could use my own agents to find the exploit just by knowing roughly what it was about and so could have been exploiting it well before the public patch was available! Given that just the rumour of a security issue seems enough to give attackers enough info to find new exploits, we’re going to need to change the way we deal with security responses in open source. Simon Willison comments: Anil points out that this rate of discovery appears incompatible with existing open source embargo pract...

item.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Rotting Squid on a Beached California Boat
item.description: Smells awful: But an estimated 30 to 50 tons of dead squid remain inside the boat’s catch tank, where they have been decomposing for days. “That is nasty. I wouldn’t want to do that,” said commercial fisherman Dick Ogg of the Bodega Bay Fishermen’s Marketing Association. Ogg said anyone familiar with the fishing industry understands what happens when a large catch sits for an extended period. “If you think about what happens after four or five days, it’s a gooey mess,” he said. The odor has become a defining feature of the operation, and the beach remains closed to the public while crews work...

item.title: Microsoft’s Patching
item.description: Once a month, Microsoft pushes a security update to all Windows users. Tomorrow’s is a new record: Microsoft’s patch for September is a doozy, with a record number of roughly 972 vulnerabilities fixed and 112 of them meeting the high critical-severity threshold. It was only two months ago that Microsoft patched a then-record 570 vulnerabilities. Then, last month, Microsoft patched some 620 of them. Google and other companies have also published record numbers of vulnerabilities in recent months. Two weeks ago, OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, and 100 companies and org...

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted email message that contains malicious SQL statements through an affected device. item.title: 25 Years of Mass Surveillance Is Enough
item.description: This essay was written with Cindy Cohn, and originally appeared in Lawfare. One of the many legacies of the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11 is the government-wide shift from targeted surveillance—such as individual wiretaps or pen register/trap and trace orders—to mass surveillance techniques—such as tapping into the internet backbone or mass collection of telephone or internet metadata. The legal and technical architecture of modern mass surveillance, initially framed as a necessary defense against terrorist threats, has grown far beyond that justification and national security in general. Mass...

New Attack Against RSA
item.description: ArsTechnica is reporting on a “new” attack against RSA, one that bypasses factoring. First, this attack isn’t new. The original research is from 2007. What is new is the implementation. Second, it is a forgery attack. It allows an attacker to forge digital signatures. It does not recover the private key from the public key. Third, the attack only works against pure signatures. That is, signatures without any formatting or padding. This is not generally how we use RSA in practice. Fourth, speed is all relative. This is not a polynomial-time algorithm; it’s a subexponential-time algorithm. But i...

item.title: I Want Better Reporting on AI Genie Behavior
item.description: AI systems are regularly completing tasks in ways that their prompters don’t want or intend. Some of them are disturbing, and some of them are dangerous. This is something I’ve been calling “genie behavior,” because I think that really gets at the core of what’s happening. I wish the popular press would report on this better. I don’t like the “going rogue” framing because it deflects the responsibility from the prompters—often the AI companies themselves. And now, pretty much anything off-script is being called “hacking.” Take, for example, the recent stories of one of OpenAI’s models hacking ...

item.title: Why AI agents are like the dog that pushed kids into the Seine
item.description: There is an interesting story about a French dog on the banks of the Seine river that helps us understand misbehaving AI agents. The dog is trained to save children from drowning. He succeeds and is rewarded, becoming an overnight sensation. He saves another child a week later. Not long after, someone witnesses the dog actually push a child into the river, jumping in to “save” him. The dog did not understand that it was being rewarded for keeping children safe, not for pulling them out of water. AI agent failures also live in this gap, where the focus is on the shortest path to fulfill th...

item.title: We are fighting phishing at the wrong layer
item.description: I timed an attacker once. From registering a domain to having it delegated, certificated and serving a live credential-harvesting page took under 24 minutes, and 12 of those were spent waiting on nameservers. I keep coming back to that number, because it quietly indicts most of what we do about phishing. We block domains. We feed them to our gateways and our DNS filters and our threat intel platforms; we measure how many we have blocked, and we report the figure to a board that finds it reassuring. An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Network Driver Interface Specification (NDIS) when ndis.sys fails to check the length of a buffer prior to copying memory to it.
To exploit the vulnerability, in a local attack scenario, an attacker could run a specially crafted application to elevate the attacker's privilege level. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run processes in an elevated context. However, an attacker must first gain access to the local system with the ability to execute a malicious application in order to exploit this vulnerability.

item.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Arbitrary File Write Vulnerability
item.description: A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system. This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system. Cisco ...

item.title: USN-8929-1: Bind vulnerabilities
item.description:
Zuyao Xu and Xiang Li discovered that Bind incorrectly handled certain malformed DNSKEY records. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Bind to consume resources, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-8677)
Yuxiao Wu, Yunyi Zhang, Baojun Liu, and Haixin Duan discovered that Bind incorrectly accepted certain records from answers. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform a cache poisoning attack. This issue only affected Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-40778)

It was discovered that OpenSSH's sftp client incorrectly handled paths returned by the server during a recursive copy operation. A remote attacker controlling the server could possibly use this issue to write files to unintended locations. (CVE-2026-106552)

item.description:

item.title: USN-8908-2: BlueZ regression
item.description:
USN-8908-1 fixed vulnerabilities in BlueZ. Unfortunately, that update introduced a regression in the A2DP profile: cached remote stream endpoints were no longer loaded at startup, which could cause Bluetooth audio devices to fail to reconnect automatically or to fall back to low-quality audio profiles. This update fixes the problem.
We apologize for the inconvenience.

item.title: USN-8930-1: U-Boot vulnerabilities
item.description:
Shahriyar Jalayeri and Mehrun P. Hunter discovered that U-Boot incorrectly handled certain NFS READ and NFS READLINK responses. An attacker could possibly use this issue to trigger a buffer overflow, resulting in a denial of service or arbitrary code execution. (CVE-2026-74220, CVE-2026-74221)
Shahriyar Jalayeri and Mehrun P. Hunter discovered that U-Boot incorrectly handled certain HTTP data storage failures in its lwIP implementation. An attacker could possibly use this issue to trigger a use-after-free, resulting in a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu ...

item.title: USN-8926-1: urllib3 vulnerabilities
item.description:
Yu-Fu Fu, Seth Larson and Yonatan Magier discovered that urllib3 did not correctly handle certain certificate validations. An attacker could possibly use this issue to observe or modify forwarded traffic. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-97687)
Martin Desrumaux discovered that urllib3 did not correctly handle decoding certain deflate responses. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-97688)

item.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
item.description: This is a problem: Any open model whose weights have been edited can carry a backdoor, whether it’s a task-specific fine-tune, a merged adapter or an abliterated build. We have abliterated models in the title because it’s the most popular reason people download modified weights without verifying what’s inside. Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model’s ability to refuse. You find the direction in the weights that carries “no” and subtract it. The model then answers things a safety-tuned version would turn down. It began as a research trick and it’s now routine before people up...

item.title: Air Force personnel's use of infected USB drives led to major malware breach
item.description: A significant security lapse within the U.S. Air Force in the early 2000s, involving the widespread use of personal USB drives for classified mission data, ultimately led to a major malware breach in 2008.

item.title: Israeli ad company secretly aided spyware delivery, report finds
item.description: An Israeli advertising company, DiscoverTech, has been secretly facilitating the placement of spyware on popular websites, enabling cyberattacks against at least 45 devices at Al Jazeera.

item.title: TSA faces new audit revealing weaknesses in sensitive data access controls
item.description: A recent Department of Homeland Security (DHS) inspector general audit has uncovered significant vulnerabilities in the Transportation Security Administration’s (TSA) controls over access to sensitive information, raising concerns about potential unauthorized access and data compromise.

item.title: Silent Lynx targets CIS government organizations with new attack chains
item.description: The threat actor Silent Lynx has been attributed to a fresh set of attacks targeting government organizations across the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

item.title: New infostealer targets AI coding assistant credentials
item.description: New versions of the Aoki infostealer are targeting credential and session files used by popular AI coding assistants, a new report by Symantec warned.

item.title: GhostAction campaign escalates, targeting over 30,000 GitHub repositories
item.description: The credential-theft campaign known as GhostAction has significantly increased its activity, impacting more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations on GitHub.

item.title: Proxyjacking campaign exploits vulnerabilities to monetize internet connections
item.description: A proxyjacking campaign has impacted devices in 34 countries, monetizing victims’ internet connections through a commercial residential proxy network by installing Pawns.app on devices without the owners’ consent.

item.title: Xbow spent $40K on AI and cracked Google Chrome wide open
item.description: A chain of vulnerabilities in Google’s Chrome browser could have enabled researchers to take control of one billion Windows machines worldwide — and it cost them just $40,000 in AI compute time to discover it. Researchers at Xbow USA worked for six days on developing the exploit, which earned them a $250,000 bug bounty from Google, the first under the new 2026 rules. They chose OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol for the task to demonstrate what’s possible with a publicly available model rather than a specialist security implementation. They used it to search Chrome’s source code, test ideas, and build ...

item.title: Cybersecurity incident at BAE Systems disrupts US bankruptcy court system
item.description: The outage has stopped official bankruptcy notices nationwide since Oct. 9, with no cause or restoration date announced. The post Cybersecurity incident at BAE Systems disrupts US bankruptcy court system appeared first on CyberScoop.

item.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
item.description:
Written by: Tyler McLellan
Introduction Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant investigated a software supply chain compromise campaign targeting the update infrastructure belonging to AOMEI Technology between April 2026 and July 2026. The threat actor conducted repeated, short-burst configuration tampering against AOMEI origin servers. Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions. item.title: Researchers Demonstrate OpenBSD Root Exploit Chaining 37-Year-Old Shared-Memory Bug
item.description: A local privilege escalation exploit published today gains root on OpenBSD 7.9 by chaining a roughly 37-year-old integer overflow with a separate kernel flaw, bypassing OpenBSD's KARL kernel-address randomization and its SMAP and SMEP hardware protections. Security firm Calif, which found and reported the flaws, published a detailed writeup and full proof-of-concept code after OpenBSD shipped...

The following CVEs are assigned: CVE-2026-58094.

item.title: ZDI-26-783: LibreOffice PDF File Parsing Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
item.description: This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of LibreOffice. The following CVEs are assigned: CVE-2026-63273.

item.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
item.description: Interesting research: Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based route...

item.description:
CVSSv3 Score:
9.8
CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

item.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
item.description: Interesting research: “AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities” Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. item.title: Officials seize domain of top bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine
item.description: The Russian-speaking cybercrime storefront was among the most active bulletproof hosting providers this year to date, receiving almost one-fifth of all illicit-attributed inflow tracked by researchers. The post Officials seize domain of top bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine appeared first on CyberScoop.

item.title: Smashing Security podcast #490: How Jared Kushner’s iPhone was allegedly hacked twice
item.description:
Dutch spies, Russian hackers and Jared Kushner’s iPhone. It sounds like the ingredients for a thriller, but according to claims in a new book the US President's son-in-law may have been hacked twice. Is any of it true, and what does it tell us about the phones in our pockets?
Meanwhile, James Ball explains that of the internet’s most trusted security keys were protected by numbers so small that one of them was... four. Yes, "4". And then, of course, to make the week worse we suffered a PHPocalpyse...
Plus, Chuck Randolph of 360 Privacy explains how the internet has made it scarily easy to pu...

item.title: Upwind raises $400M after walking away from Datadog acquisition offer
item.description: The cloud security startup raised a Series C at a $3.8B valuation, instead of selling itself for the same price.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
item.description: A vulnerability in the peering authentication in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Validator, formerly SD-WAN vBond, could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system. This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could all...

item.title: After the breach: Uncovering the full scope of the attack
item.description: Following an incident, every major decision depends on knowing exactly what happened.

item.title: Federal Election Commission systems taken offline following cyberattack
item.description: The Federal Election Commission has taken multiple filing systems offline following a targeted cyberattack, according to a recent report by Nextgov.

item.title: Leak site publishes data on more than 41,000 DHS employees obtained by hacktivists
item.description: The Department of Peace group shared it with Swiss hacker/journalist maia arson crimew and DDoSecrets put it online. The post Leak site publishes data on more than 41,000 DHS employees obtained by hacktivists appeared first on CyberScoop.

item.title: Upwind Security raises $400 million to scale cloud and AI security platform
item.description: Upwind Security Inc. has secured $400 million in new funding, bringing its total valuation to $3.8 billion as it expands its automated cloud security operations, based on information published by Silicon Angle.

item.title: Discord to index discoverable server discussions for web search
